clue.text: Example of native labour that's not so hot at first

indicators.note: at first tells the solver to place the cooler piece ahead of the abbreviation

parts.note: cool describes something not so hot, between warm and cold
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A remark that some native labour is not very impressive at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so hot' sounds like faint praise of the labour; 'at first' sets the temperature word ahead of the Latin abbreviation. The defined word is dated and now offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The term historically denoted an unskilled hired labourer from Asia, now considered offensive.

clue.text: Part of one's goal to do so, sailing from harbour?

definitions.meaning: the horizontal beam across the top of goalposts

definitions.text: to do so, sailing from harbour?
definitions.meaning: a ship leaving port passes over the sandbank at the harbour mouth

explanation.surface: Part of the goal, or what a ship does leaving port.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a goal's top beam, and going over a sandbank when putting to sea.

clue.text: Murder scene as reported to Hamlet

definitions.text: Murder scene as reported to Hamlet

parts.words: Murder scene as reported to Hamlet
parts.note: the Ghost tells Hamlet he was killed while sleeping among his fruit trees

explanation.surface: A crime location described to Shakespeare's Danish prince.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, the Ghost says Claudius poisoned him while he slept in his garden of fruit trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of fruit trees, where Hamlet's father was said to have died.

clue.text: One politician, note, on the ball showing current resistance

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP stands for Member of Parliament
E is a musical note
a ball is a dance, a formal gathering for dancing

explanation.surface: A politician who is sharp and alert shows resistance to the current trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the ball' sounds like alertness but is DANCE (a ball). The page prints 'politican', a misprint not affecting the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedance measures opposition to alternating electric current in a circuit.

clue.text: Lido fashion from Westminster district followed by many, clubs perhaps?

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode for Westminster, the 1 read as the letter I
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
clubs is one example of a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A fashion seen at the lido coming from Westminster and taken up by many nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the postcode district covering Westminster in London, its digit taken as the letter I. A lido is a British public open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece bathing costume is what fashion dictates for swimmers at an outdoor pool.

clue.text: The victims of Joshua's long-winded attack

definitions.text: The victims of Joshua's long-winded attack

parts.words: The victims of Joshua's long-winded attack
parts.note: in the Bible Joshua's priests blew trumpets, a wind attack, and the city's defences fell

explanation.surface: Those who suffered from a biblical leader's lengthy, breathy assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long-winded' sounds like tedious, but means trumpets blown for a long time: in the Book of Joshua the blasts brought the city's defences down.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortifications of a biblical city fell when Joshua's trumpets sounded.

clue.text: Author on the square?

definitions.meaning: A. E. W. ... was an English novelist
Freemasons are said to be on the square, and builders work with a set square

explanation.surface: A writer who is honest and straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an English novelist's surname, and a stoneworker or Freemason using a square.

clue.text: Set free one soul in torment

indicators.note: torment suggests writhing, so the letters of the words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Releasing a soul that is suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in torment' rearranges ONE SOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To release or let go, an old synonym of loosen.

clue.text: Frugality causes most of the dissension in the plant

definitions.meaning: sea pink, a coastal flowering plant

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: a rift is a split or dissension between people

explanation.surface: Being stingy leads to most of the arguments at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory but is a flower, sea pink; 'most of' trims THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful saving of money is the sense of frugality, and sea pink is the flower's other name.

clue.text: Requests for first courses, in discipline of course

definitions.meaning: orders for starters, the opening dishes of a meal
jockeys at a racecourse are under the starter's control before the off

explanation.surface: Diners order starters while strictly following a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' shifts from a meal course to a racecourse, where horses line up 'under starter's orders'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: diners' requests for appetisers, and the official's instructions to racehorses before a race begins.

clue.text: Italic cop suffers fracture of this bone

indicators.note: a fractured thing is broken up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman of Italian style breaks a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers fracture of' breaks up ITALIC COP into the answer; the bone wordplay fits the surface's injury.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the bone forming the back and base of the skull.

clue.text: Describing our system in two notes? Right

parts.note: soh is a note of the sol-fa scale, spelt here so
lah is the next note of the sol-fa scale, spelt here la

explanation.surface: Explaining a musical system using just two notes, and being correct about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two notes' gives two sol-fa notes side by side; the musical surface hides the astronomical sense of 'our system'.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planetary system is the one centred on the Sun, so an adjective from the Latin sun word describes it.

clue.text: Manxman for instance beheaded for calumny

indicators.note: beheaded means the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a Manxman lives on the Isle of Man, so he is one example of an island dweller

explanation.surface: A man from the Isle of Man is executed for spreading lies.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manxman comes from the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, so is an ISLANDER; 'beheaded' drops the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is a false and damaging spoken statement about someone, a synonym.

clue.text: Farewell celebration. — for an errant footballer?

definitions.meaning: a party held to wish someone well on departure
a player who commits a bad foul is ordered from the pitch by the referee

explanation.surface: A leaving party, or what a misbehaving footballer gets.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a farewell gathering, and a dismissal from the field for foul play in football.

clue.text: Forest endlessly burning

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ardent means burning, from the Latin for blazing

explanation.surface: A woodland fire that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Arden is the woodland setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It; 'endlessly' cuts the T from ARDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Arden is a named English woodland, famous as the setting of a Shakespeare comedy.

clue.text: Like the law, when the police appear finally

indicators.note: the police appear within the word for finally, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: end is what comes finally, the close
the force is a common British name for the police

explanation.surface: The law only takes effect once the police turn up at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear' signals one piece set inside the other. In Britain 'the Force' is a usual name for a police service.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws are imposed and made binding, which is what applying them by authority means.

clue.text: Goes about the island as one delivering the goods

parts.note: rounds are circuits someone goes about making
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Someone tours the island making deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes about' suggests wandering, but means making a delivery round; the island is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who calls at houses on a regular route bringing milk or bread.

clue.text: Struggles with Wales, using others to replace a loss

indicators.note: to replace means one letter is swapped out for the new word

parts.note: taken as written
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Wales struggles, bringing in other players to make up for a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others to replace a' swaps the A in WALES for REST; 'a loss' reads as a defeat but means the A is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapples or contends hard, as wrestlers do.

clue.text: Landlord's story about a riotous scene

definitions.note: read as landlord is, a noun naming the person

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: riotous suggests disorder, so the letters of scene are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub landlord tells a tale about a rowdy scene in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riotous' makes CENSE from SCENE and 'about' wraps the story round it. In Britain a pub landlord holds the licence to sell alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A British publican is the holder of the alcohol licence for the premises, so the landlord is this.

clue.text: A young devil learning to beg

parts.note: an imp is a small or young devil
lore is traditional learning

explanation.surface: A naughty child learning how to plead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A young devil' is IMP, the A simply part of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead with someone earnestly, a synonym of beseech.

clue.text: Such is the case of The Times leaders

definitions.text: Such is the case of The Times leaders

parts.words: Such is the case of The Times leaders
parts.note: the first letters of the words The and Times are capitals, and case here means typographic case rather than a situation

explanation.surface: A remark about the editorials in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like newspaper editorials; it means the opening letters of The Times, which are capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are printed in the higher case, the top tray of type in old printing.

clue.text: Seen in concert — tattered rag of software

indicators.note: seen in means the scrambled letters sit inside the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

indicators.note: tattered means torn to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ragged-looking figure turns up at a concert, apparently a computer thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattered' makes GRA from RAG and 'Seen in' sets it inside the concert, a promenade concert like London's BBC Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: A program is a set of coded instructions run by a computer, the American spelling used in computing.

clue.text: Far from broad sort of artist

indicators.note: sort here means to arrange, so the letters of the word are reordered

explanation.surface: An artist who is a narrow-minded type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective meaning narrow or tight, the sense in strait-laced.

clue.text: Barman's part, set for revision

definitions.note: read as barman is, a noun naming the person

indicators.note: revision means reworking, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A barman learns his part, which has been set for him to revise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for revision' rearranges PART SET; 'Barman's' reads as 'barman is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for someone who draws beer from the taps in a pub, a synonym.

clue.text: Tricky situation, this spot, having over-indulged

definitions.meaning: a difficult position is described as this kind of spot

explanation.surface: A drinker in a tricky spot after overdoing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: 'in a tight spot' means in trouble, and it is slang for drunk.

clue.text: Among nameless givers not seen in the open

parts.note: in means among, within a group

indicators.note: nameless means the abbreviation for name, the letter N, is removed

parts.note: donors are people who give

explanation.surface: Anonymous donors who keep out of public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' strips N (the abbreviation for name) from DONORS to leave DOORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside a building means being out of the open air.

clue.text: "Having pray'd together, we Will go with you ___" (Herrick)

definitions.text: "Having pray'd together, we Will go with you ___" (Herrick)

parts.words: "Having pray'd together, we Will go with you ___" (Herrick)
parts.note: the missing word completes the closing line of Robert Herrick's poem To Daffodils, meaning in company

explanation.surface: A line of seventeenth-century verse with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation comes from Herrick's poem To Daffodils; the blank is a fill-in-the-blank clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in company with someone, accompanying them on their way.

clue.text: In passing, alter helm without time to go after record

indicators.note: to go after means this piece follows the record in the answer

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the word for time
alter means change, so the letters of helm are rearranged

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: While passing, a sailor changes the helm without delay after setting a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter' makes HEML from HELM; 'without' means outside, wrapping it round the time word, and 'to go after' puts all that behind the record.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting lasts only briefly, a thing merely passing.

clue.text: Work on subject of international agreements, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and sounds alike

parts.note: treaties are formal agreements between nations

explanation.surface: Writing a study about treaties between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: the word for international agreements sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written study dealing systematically with a topic.

clue.text: Ill-feeling created if one has total rejection

parts.note: an is an archaic word for if, as in Shakespeare
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: rejection means the word for total is turned back

parts.note: a sum is a total

explanation.surface: Resentment arises when someone has everything thrown back.
explanation.walkthrough: AN for 'if' is old usage ("an it please you"); 'rejection' turns SUM into MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is hostility or enmity towards someone, a synonym.
